capitals.name: Kuwait City
capitals.note: The Kuwait page: 'Capital and largest city: Kuwait City'.

keyframe_review.note: 5,500 km2, 16 cells around Kuwait Bay, for 1757-1804: the Sheikhdom's core, read as holding from 1752 (the Kuwait page: 'the territory became known as the Sheikdom of Kuwait in 1752'; the History page: Sabah I's selection 'is usually dated to 1752'). Infobox area of modern Kuwait 17,818 km2 (Kuwait page). The shape is 0.31 of it, beyond a factor of two, but no page defines the Sheikhdom's extent before 1913 (the Kuwait page has 'no explicit sentence defining Kuwait's territorial extent before 1913') and the modern borders were fixed only in 1913-1923, so the shape is kept as a core, not a frontier.

Unverified for its 20-vertex outline (5,421 km2, 1805-1819), a slight variant of the 1757 core. The History page has Abdullah I ruling 1776-1814, a period that left Sabah rule 'secure'; no page opened has a territorial change in 1805 or 1820. The Emirate of Diriyah touches Kuwait in 1791-1819 (Cliopatria).

Unverified (5,500 km2, 1820-1872): the 1757 core again. 'The Ottoman military intervention of 1871 was not effectively pursued'; the Kuwait row ends in 1872 although Kuwait goes on under 'nominal' Ottoman vassalage (1871) and in the Basra Vilayet (1875), so a new 1873 keyframe continues it.

correction.text: the Sheikhdom's core unchanged: 'a nominal vassal of the Ottoman Empire in 1871 ... included in the Basra Vilayet' (1875), then under British protection from the agreement of 23 January 1899

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Kuwait shape for 1873-1960. The Ottoman vassalage of 1871 and the British protectorate of 1899 (Britain took responsibility for foreign policy and security, with a 15,000-rupee subsidy) change the suzerain, not the land.

correction.text: The Anglo-Ottoman Convention of 29 July 1913 gave the sheikh authority within an 80 km radius of Kuwait City, 'which included the islands of Auhah, Bubiyan, Failaka, Kubbar, Mashian, and Warbah', with a further 100 km zone for tribute and taxes; clipped to today's lines because the Uqair and 1923 borders cut the rest off

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 38 cells. The Sheikhdom of Kuwait page says the 1913 draft 'was not signed before World War I, so its status is unclear'. The 80 km circle takes in Iraqi and Saudi land that the 1922-23 lines left outside, so it is intersected with the later State of Kuwait shape.

correction.text: Kuwait within the Uqair line with Najd (2 December 1922) and, from 19 April 1923, with 'the outer line of the convention' as the Iraq border, which 'limited Iraq's access to the Persian Gulf at 58 km'; the Neutral Zone half is shared and left out

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, the 1961 shape (14,031 km2, 0.79 of the infobox area) carried back to 1923. The History page: 'On 19 April 1923, Britain recognized the outer green line as the Iraq-Kuwait border'; Iraq accepted it in 1932.

14,031 km2 for 1961-1972 against 17,818 on the infobox (0.79): modern Kuwait without its half of the Neutral Zone, which was still shared. 'In June 1961, Kuwait became independent with the end of the British protectorate' (infobox 19 June 1961).

correction.text: The shape is unchanged but Kuwait's half of the Neutral Zone belongs to it from 25 July 1966, not 1973: 'On 7 July 1965, the two governments signed an agreement to partition the zone' and it 'took effect on 25 July 1966'

keyframe_review.note: 17,395 km2 (0.98 of the infobox area). Years change only: Cliopatria adds the 3,288 km2 half in 1973; the demarcation took effect on 18 December 1969 and was ratified on 18 January 1970.

17,395 km2, the same shape as 1973 for 1987-1989; the Cliopatria State of Kuwait row ends in 1989 and the Kuwait row resumes in 1991; the invasion was on 2 August 1990 (Kuwait page), so this is a row boundary, not a change of state.

correction.text: Kuwait unchanged but occupied by Iraq from 2 August 1990; 'Iraq annexed Kuwait on 8 August 1990'; drawn hatched (rule 4) by the ledger's occupation events

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria has no Kuwait shape for 1990 (State of Kuwait ends 1989, Kuwait resumes 1991). The annexation was not recognised, so the land stays Kuwaiti and occupied.

17,395 km2 for 1991-2023 (0.98 of the infobox). UN Resolution 687 'demarcated the border' with Iraq, which Iraq formally accepted in November 1994; the page gives no area change and the shape is kept.

ledger.note: 1752: the Utub choose Sabah I as sheikh of Kuwait. 'This selection is usually dated to 1752' (History of Kuwait); the Kuwait page: 'the territory became known as the Sheikdom of Kuwait in 1752'. Kuwait City was then 'a small fishing village' and the Utub took control after the decline of the Bani Khalid through marriage alliances.

region.text: the 80 km radius around Kuwait City of the 1913 convention, clipped to today's Kuwait

ledger.note: 29 July 1913: the Anglo-Ottoman Convention defines Kuwait. Britain and the Ottomans agreed 'defining Kuwait as an autonomous kaza of the Ottoman Empire' with the sheikh's authority over an 80 km radius 'which included the islands of Auhah, Bubiyan, Failaka, Kubbar, Mashian, and Warbah' (date from the Kuwait infobox). The draft 'was not signed before World War I' (Sheikhdom of Kuwait page), so the land is the claim of record.

region.text: Al Jahra and the Red Fort, west of Kuwait City

ledger.note: 10 October 1920: the Ikhwan attack Kuwait at Jahra. 'The battle took place in Al Jahra, west of Kuwait City on 10 October 1920', about 4,000 Ikhwan against some 2,000 defenders, during the Kuwait-Najd War (sporadic clashes in 1919-1920 per the Sheikhdom page).

region.text: the Kuwait-Najd frontier west of Kuwait City

ledger.note: 2 December 1922: Uqair fixes the Kuwait-Najd boundary. The Uqair protocol set the Kuwait-Najd boundaries (Cox imposed it; 'Kuwait was not permitted any role in the Uqair agreement'); the Uqair Convention is dated 2 December 1922 on the Neutral Zone page. The page does not date the end of the fighting, so the treaty is the end.

region.text: Kuwait's half of the Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone (the 5,770 km2 zone 'carved out by the British in 1922'): the land Cliopatria adds to the State of Kuwait shape in 1973

ledger.note: 2 December 1922: the Neutral Zone is created. The Uqair Convention 'established the border and left the zone undefined' (5,770 km2); 'the Government of Najd and Kuwait will share equal rights until' a later agreement. Drawn as the blend of the two states.

region.text: the western part of Kuwait beyond the 1913 radius, inside 'the outer green line'

ledger.note: 19 April 1923: Britain fixes the Iraq-Kuwait line. Sir Percy Cox's government 'recognised the outer line of the convention as the border between Iraq and Kuwait'; the History page: it 'limited Iraq's access to the Persian Gulf at 58 km'. Iraq accepted the line in 1932. The land is what lies inside that line beyond the 80 km radius of 1913.

19 June 1961: Kuwait becomes independent. 'Independence from the United Kingdom: 19 June 1961' (infobox); 'In June 1961, Kuwait became independent with the end of the British protectorate' of 1899. Cliopatria's Kuwait row becomes 'State of Kuwait'; the state and its colour continue.

region.text: Kuwait's half of the Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone (the 5,770 km2 zone 'carved out by the British in 1922'): the land Cliopatria adds to the State of Kuwait shape in 1973

ledger.note: 25 July 1966: the Neutral Zone is partitioned. 'On 7 July 1965, the two governments signed an agreement to partition the zone' and it 'took effect on 25 July 1966'; demarcation took effect on 18 December 1969 and the agreement was ratified on 18 January 1970.

region.text: Kuwait's half of the Saudi-Kuwaiti Neutral Zone (the 5,770 km2 zone 'carved out by the British in 1922'): the land Cliopatria adds to the State of Kuwait shape in 1973

ledger.note: 25 July 1966: Kuwait takes its half of the Neutral Zone. The page does not say how the zone was divided; Cliopatria adds the 3,288 km2 southern part to Kuwait in 1973. Confidence 2: the page names no part of the zone as Kuwait's (review me-10-d).

2 August 1990: Iraq invades and annexes Kuwait. 'The invasion of Kuwait and annexation by Iraq took place on 2 August 1990'; 'Iraq annexed Kuwait on 8 August 1990'. The annexation was never recognised, so the land is shown as occupied, not lost.

28 February 1991: Kuwait is liberated. Infobox 'Liberation of Kuwait: 28 February 1991'; the ground assault began on 23 February 1991 and 'achieved a complete removal of Iraqi forces from Kuwait in four days' (History page).

wars.name: Kuwait-Najd War

zones.text: Jahra, where the Ikhwan attacked the Red Fort on 10 October 1920

wars.outcome: Sporadic border clashes in 1919-1920 and the Battle of Jahra (10 October 1920); settled by the Uqair Protocol of 1922, which set the Kuwait-Najd boundary and created the Neutral Zone.
wars.note: Years: clashes 1919-1920 (Sheikhdom page); 1922 is the Uqair Convention (2 December 1922, Neutral Zone page).

wars.name: Iraqi invasion of Kuwait
wars.outcome: Iraq invaded on 2 August 1990 and annexed Kuwait on 8 August; the bombardment began on 17 January 1991 and the ground assault on 23 February; Iraqi forces were gone in four days (liberation 28 February 1991). UN Resolution 687 demarcated the border, accepted by Iraq in November 1994.
wars.note: The coalition states (the United States of America and others) are not listed as belligerents; the History page names none.

certainty.note: No page defines the Sheikhdom's extent before 1913, the 1913 convention was an unsigned draft with a further 100 km tribute zone, and the Najd frontier was open until Uqair.
The Uqair line (2 December 1922) and the Iraq line (19 April 1923, re-recognised 1932) are treaty lines; the Neutral Zone is shared and not sharp.
The Neutral Zone partition took effect 25 July 1966; UN Resolution 687 demarcated the Iraq border, accepted in November 1994.

notes: Written by me-10-d on 2026-10-25 from four pages (budget up to 5). ONE STATE, TWO CLIOPATRIA ROWS: 'Kuwait' (1757-1872, 1991-2024) and 'State of Kuwait' (1961-1989) share Wikidata Q817 and are one state with Cliopatria rows missing for 1873-1960 and 1990. This dossier covers both and adds the missing keyframes (1873, 1913, 1923, 1990). DUPLICATE TO RETIRE: history/polities/state-of-kuwait.json (written by me-10-k, which kept it separate and recorded the 1961 independence as a 'found' and the 1991 end as a 'dissolve') duplicates the 1961-1991 stretch of this dossier; the orchestrator should delete it or turn it into a pointer, and colours.json gives the two slugs different hues (#b85e31, #ca933e). PROTECTORATES AND VASSALAGE belong in the suzerain's ledger: the Ottoman Empire (Kuwait a 'nominal vassal' from 1871, in the Basra Vilayet from 1875, an 'autonomous kaza' by the 1913 draft) and the United Kingdom (the agreement of 23 January 1899, ended 19 June 1961; the History page: Britain took responsibility for foreign policy and security for 15,000 rupees a year) should carry vassal_start/vassal_end for Kuwait; the United Kingdom's dossier is kingdom-of-great-britain (eu-11). CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO NOTE: the Kuwait shape of 1757-1872 (5,500 km2) is a core, 0.31 of today's area; no page defines the earlier extent. The 1805-1819 outline is a trivial variant. NOT DONE: the Wahhabi attacks of the 1790s-1810s (the Emirate of Diriyah touches Kuwait in 1791-1819 in Cliopatria; none of the pages opened mentions them), the full list of Sabah rulers (the pages date only Sabah I 1752-1776, Abdullah I 1776-1814, Muhammad to May 1896, Mubarak 1896/97-1915, Jaber II to early 1917; no rulers strip entered), the Zand occupation of Basra 1776-1779 next door (Cliopatria's neighbours list shows it; no Kuwaiti page mentions it), the 1993 UN demarcation (no area change on the pages), Bubiyan and Warbah (inside the 1913 radius). DISAGREEMENTS: the Neutral Zone page dates the Uqair Convention 2 December 1922; the History page says 'Uqair Protocol of 1922'. The 1913 date (29 July) is the Kuwait infobox's; the Sheikhdom page says the draft was never signed. Iraq's recognition of the 1923 line is dated 1932 in both pages. The ground assault of 1991 began on 23 February; the infobox liberation date is 28 February.
